Senses.Explanation: The graphs mean “standard or grading frame” and “outside”: “beyond the norms.” In this corpus it is applied to sayings, phrases, actions, workings, and people. Recurrent combinations include “upheld beyond the norms,” “workings beyond the norms,” “a saying beyond the norms,” “a phrase beyond the norms,” “a person beyond the norms,” and “the Chan purport beyond the norms.” The records draw explicit contrasts. What is upheld beyond the norms is said not to establish grades of capacity, unlike phrases directed to middle or lower capacities. A saying beyond the norms is contrasted with explaining meaning by relying on scripture. A comment applies the term to Zhaozhou's answer “the cypress tree in the front garden,” and catalogues characterize Yunmen's house as solitary and steep, upheld beyond the norms. Records also ask directly, “What is a phrase beyond the norms?” A later comment examines and rejects Yaoshan's claim to possess workings beyond the norms, judging that it reveals what it tries to hide. The headword occurs 1,113 times across 245 allowlisted texts. The entry reports these applications and contrasts without treating the label as automatically valid.
Senses.Note: This is a corpus-wide descriptor whose application may be asserted, queried, or rejected. The curated occurrences are hall addresses, case comments, and lineage catalogues, so their speaker fields remain null.

Senses.Explanation: Literally, ‘a phrase outside the standard.’ The corpus uses it as a named class of utterance in public questioning and case appraisal. Yuanwu’s pointer says that if one can distinguish such a phrase, ‘raise one and understand three’; later in the same collection he says one must know the phrase outside the standard so that, when public cases and words are raised, one knows their place. A monk can ask directly, ‘what is a phrase outside the standard?’ and receive the answer, ‘the staff-tip points out a thousand peaks; before the Five-Phoenix Tower, listen for fine news.’ Other speakers coordinate it with ‘the upward pivot,’ contrast it with ‘the basic-function mechanism,’ or attribute it to Yunmen while saying that Yunmen and the Buddha each displayed their own style but had not yet accorded with the basis. One later discourse dismisses ‘the phrase outside the standard’ as a worn-out straw sandal alongside ‘the upward pivot’ as rotten hemp rope. Zen usage therefore bends the ordinary ‘outside the norm’ modifier into a technical phrase-class that masters request, distinguish, perform, compare with other phrase and mechanism classes, and appraise in public interviews.
Senses.Note: One corpus-wide technical phrase class. Individual answers and competing appraisals are not separate senses. The headword ‘outside the standard’ (格外) remains broader; ‘a phrase outside the standard’ (格外句) is its lexicalized phrase-class compound and is cross-referenced rather than collapsed into it.

Senses.Explanation: Literally, 'inside a ghost cave.' The phrase occurs 309 times in 122 allowed texts. The corpus repeatedly extends it as 'making a living inside a ghost cave' (鬼窟裏作活計, 164 occurrences), 'sitting inside a ghost cave' (鬼窟裏坐, 17), and 'inside a ghost cave beneath the black mountain' (黑山下鬼窟裏, 15). Dahui warns, 'take special care not to reckon inside a ghost cave' (切忌向鬼窟裏卜度), and elsewhere describes remaining motionless inside a ghost cave below the black mountain. Yuanwu writes that activity based on conscious calculation is 'making a living inside a ghost cave' and repeats the wording after 'as soon as you calculate' (纔作計較). Yunmen's record sets up a conditional choice: if the monk cannot answer, he is 'sitting inside a ghost cave.' These are the corpus's own spatial and verbal extensions of the image; the texts do not supply a separate object-definition for the cave.
Senses.Note: No required direct-definition formula was found. The headword is productive with verbs of reckoning, calculating, sitting, entering, emerging, and making a living. The common longer form adds 'below the black mountain.' The article preserves that observable usage without converting the phrase into a category not stated by the records.
